title: An HTML card that escapes its input

blocks.text: HTML templates are one of the page's main use cases, and its security answer shows the catch: `formatted()` puts text in as it is, so `<script>` from a user becomes a real script tag. Its safe version escapes the input first.
Write `Html.card(String title, String body)`. It returns these four lines joined by `\n`, with no newline after the last:

Both values are escaped before they go in: `&` becomes `&`, `<` becomes `<`, `>` becomes `>` and `"` becomes `"`. Escape `&` **first**, or the `&` of an escape made earlier would be escaped again. Every `&` is escaped, even one that already starts something like `<`: the input is text, not HTML. A single quote is left as it is.

cases.says: The title and the body fill the four-line card, with no newline at the end.
Markup in the title is escaped just as in the body.
& is escaped before the other characters, so < is never turned into &lt;.

concepts: Values put into an HTML template are escaped, & first, or user text becomes markup.
